**Observation Log:**

[TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/29 (Mon) 17:18  
[EVENT] User is planning a picnic in their local park this weekend.  
[PREFERENCE] User is wondering about bird-friendly food to attract birds.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested bird-friendly foods include:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Suet: A high-energy food made from animal fat, favorite among woodpeckers, nuthatches, and chickadees.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Sunflower seeds: Popular among cardinals, finches, and sparrows; recommended to use black oil sunflower seeds.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Fresh fruits: Sliced apples, grapes, berries, and oranges attract robins, blue jays, and woodpeckers; seeds and pits should be removed.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Nuts: Almonds, walnuts, and hazelnuts should be chopped into smaller pieces.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. Dried mealworms: Attract bluebirds, wrens, and sparrows; available at pet stores or online.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 6. Nyjer seed: Attracts finches, sparrows, and goldfinches; small size and high oil content make it an excellent energy source.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended to place food on a clean, flat surface or bird-friendly feeder, keep food fresh, and be mindful of park rules.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Encouraged user to enjoy observing birds from a safe distance.  
[EVENT] User plans to bring sunflower seeds and suet to attract woodpeckers.  
[FACT] User saw a Northern Flicker in their local park last weekend, bringing their total species count to 32.  
[PREFERENCE] User inquires if suet will attract other woodpecker species.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Confirmed that suet is likely to attract other woodpecker species, including:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Downy Woodpeckers: Common, small black-and-white birds.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Hairy Woodpeckers: Similar to Downy but larger.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Red-bellied Woodpeckers: Distinctive red cap and loud calls.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Pileated Woodpeckers: Largest woodpeckers in North America with a red crest.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Advised to place the suet feeder in an accessible spot and suggested adding peanut butter or jelly to the suet.
